title: Engineering Manager, Runtime Platform, Robot Software
descriptionHtml:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Engineering Teams

Wayve is building embodied AI that can drive any vehicle, anywhere. Our AI Driver operates onboard the vehicle in real time, supported by the application frameworks, middleware, performance capabilities and observability foundations owned by the Runtime Platform team.

This growing function is becoming a dedicated team, and you’ll be the Engineering Manager responsible for leading it. Other onboard components depend on the frameworks, inter-process communication layers, monitoring and performance capabilities your team delivers.

The team’s work is central to scaling Wayve’s AI Driver across new vehicles, OEM programes and other embodiments.

🧠 Your day-to-day

You’ll lead a single team and be accountable for its delivery, engagement, resourcing, roadmap and performance. People leadership will be your first priority: you’ll coach and develop engineers, maintain a healthy and high-performing team, and lead hiring and onboarding as the team grows.

You’ll combine this with strong technical judgement, establishing direction across latency, profiling, real-time scheduling, middleware and observability. Working closely with technical leads and stakeholders, you’ll own the outcomes of the team’s technical decisions and ensure its roadmap supports Wayve’s broader goals.

You’ll also act as the team’s escalation point, proactively identifying and resolving risks, dependencies and delivery challenges.

🧩 What you’ll be working on

  • Leading and developing the team: Run effective one-to-ones, set clear expectations, provide regular high-quality feedback, manage performance and support career development against Wayve’s career framework

  • Hiring and building the team: Own hiring and onboarding, ensure the right people are in the right roles, and shape the team’s culture and ways of working

  • Driving execution: Staff committed programmes, align the roadmap with available resources, prioritise effectively and hold the team accountable for delivery, quality and operational reliability

  • Setting technical direction: Establish a clear, holistic direction and ownership of technology-roadmap milestones in partnership with technical leads and stakeholders

  • Owning runtime foundations: Guide the team’s work across system design, application frameworks, middleware and IPC, performance optimisation, measurement and observability

  • Enabling new vehicle platforms: Support additional vehicle platforms through incremental development while minimizing performance degradation

  • Strengthening quality and iteration: Implement and maintain strong continuous integration, hardware-in-the-loop testing and internal quality gates

  • Collaborating across Wayve: Partner with Vehicle Software, model development, hardware and OEM programe teams

  • Unblocking delivery: Cascade the roadmap, surface risks and dependencies early, and act as the team’s point of escalation

🙌 You should apply if

  • You have a strong track record of leading, growing, engaging and retaining a high-performing software or systems team

  • You have experience hiring, coaching, providing feedback, managing performance and supporting engineers’ career development

  • You have owned a team roadmap and delivered through others, including planning, prioritisation, resourcing and accountability for quality and operational reliability

  • You have hands-on experience architecting and delivering embedded software shipped in a physical product to real customers

  • You understand high-performance, low-latency embedded software developed in C++ and can earn the trust of senior systems engineers without needing to be the team’s top individual contributor

  • You understand profiling, benchmarking, latency, throughput, memory-bandwidth analysis and real-time scheduling on embedded Linux

  • You have a strong understanding of middleware used in high-throughput, real-time or robotics systems, including the trade-offs across vendors and platforms

  • You can establish direction and deliver through influence across multiple stakeholder teams

The following experience would be useful but is not required:

  • Automotive, robotics or another safety-relevant, real-time domain

  • QNX, a microkernel architecture or another real-time operating system

  • Profiling tools such as pprof/gperftools, perf, Nsight or NVLumo

  • Observability platforms such as OpenTelemetry, Grafana or Datadog

  • NVIDIA Orin or Thor compute platforms

  • Qualcomm compute platforms

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay. If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end-to-end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real-world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalize and improve at scale.

Instead of relying on hand-coded rules or pre-mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency.

We believe autonomy represents a once-in-a-generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars and from human-driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware-agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2+ through to L4 as our core AI model scales.

In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real-world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach: building generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer and more intelligent future of mobility.

💻 How we work—location and flexible working

This is a full-time role based in our London office.

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated offices and workshops with focused time working remotely.

We also operate core working hours, allowing you to determine the schedule that works best for you and your team. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together alongside the flexibility to do their best work.

🔍 The interview process

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial recruiter conversation

  • Competency interviews — Leadership & Management and Runtime Platform Domain interviews; approximately two hours in total

  • Deep-dive interviews — Hiring Manager, Software Systems Design and Code Review interviews; approximately three hours in total

  • Final interview — mission and values alignment; approximately one hour

We’ll explain each format in advance and work around your availability.

Wayve is committed to creating an inclusive interview experience. If you require any accommodations or adjustments to participate fully in the process, please let us know.

What’s in it for you?

Benefits vary by location.

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long-term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and opportunities to work hands-on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets, with support for training, conferences and professional growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits, including health insurance, dental coverage, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension support where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

 

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

title: Engineering Team Lead, Managed K8s
descriptionHtml:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The team

Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible — compute orchestration, Kubernetes, bare metal, storage, networking, and the datacenter fleet that runs it all.

We run it all on our own metal, our own network, our own datacenters — which means when something breaks, the fix is ours to write.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on and shape the team building it.

The Role

This is a people-leadership role from day one. You will manage the team — hiring, coaching, performance, growth paths, honest feedback — while staying close to the code: roughly half your time in architecture decisions and the hardest technical problems the team faces, the other half leading your squad. If you are looking for a senior IC role, this is not it.

You will own our Kubernetes product end to end: a metal-to-on-demand platform built on in-house infrastructure, with GPU support for training, inference, and general-purpose compute.

Kubernetes is our product, not just our platform — we run it on infrastructure we own end to end. You will decide how the control plane scales, how GPUs get scheduled, and how quickly a rack of bare metal becomes an on-demand cluster a customer can use. The decisions you make here shape how our infrastructure scales from today's footprint to a gigawatt, and how we turn frontier AI research into production systems used by millions.

This is a role for an engineer who leads from the front because that is where the work is, not because management was the next rung on the ladder.

What You Will Do

  • Design and ship the control plane. You build alongside your team and own the architecture and the hardest implementation decisions — scheduling, operators, provisioning, node lifecycle.

  • Grow the engineers, not just the software. You set the standard for ownership, remove the obstacles in their way, and coach them past their comfort zone until the work they ship surprises them.

  • Own the reliability of the Kubernetes control plane. It is the team's headline KPI. You make the calls when it breaks at 3am, and your engineers learn from how you do it.

  • Shrink the distance from metal to on-demand. Provisioning a cluster should be minutes of automation, not weeks of tickets.

  • Partner with Product Managers to set priorities, scope initiatives, and make the technical and business tradeoffs.

  • Own people management for the team: hiring, performance, growth paths, and honest feedback — the leadership work that never becomes someone else's job.

  • Define the team's processes and execution rituals as it grows.

What We're Looking For

  • 2+ years of real people leadership. You have managed engineers — hired, coached, given honest feedback, and grown them. Hands-on contribution matters here, but this role is judged on the team you build and lead, not just the code you write.

  • You have shipped production systems in Go. Not dabbled. Shipped.

  • You have run Kubernetes in anger — and ideally built parts of it: operators, schedulers, controllers. You understand what happens underneath it, and you have worked on Linux directly, not just on managed services that sit on top of it.

  • You have run GPU workloads on Kubernetes, or you are confident you can own that domain fast.

  • You think like a developer who happens to build infrastructure, not an operator who manages it. You write code other engineers depend on.

  • Extensive experience building backend or infrastructure systems.

  • You have partnered with product, design, and business teams to ship software that reached real users.

  • A low-ego, team-first mindset. We care less about your exact domain and more about whether you are the kind of technical force other engineers want to work alongside.

What We Offer

Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

title: Engineering Technician
descriptionHtml:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

 

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

 

YOUR IMPACT

At Proxima Fusion, we're developing the world's leading stellarator technology. To turn cutting-edge designs into reality, we need skilled technicians who can bring complex, first-of-a-kind hardware to life. As a Technician at Proxima Fusion, you'll work hands-on with Proxima-designed components, magnets, mechanical assemblies and other critical systems, supporting their build, assembly, integration and testing.

Working closely with Engineering, Manufacturing and Quality, you'll help turn ambitious designs into reliable hardware, solve practical challenges on the shop floor and contribute to developing the processes and tooling needed to build Alpha. This is a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced engineering and hands-on manufacturing, helping build one of Europe's most ambitious engineering projects.

 

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Build, assemble and modify prototypes, experimental hardware, custom tooling and development rigs for engineering and special projects across the programme.

  • Turn engineering drawings, models, and sketches into practical hardware. Clarify missing requirements and agree the build approach with the responsible engineer before committing to uncertain or irreversible steps.

  • Fabricate and adapt components using fitting, cutting, drilling, soldering, bonding and assembly techniques within your competence. Coordinate specialist machining, welding or other work when needed.

  • Identify buildability issues early, including tolerance stacks, inaccessible fasteners, component fit and assembly sequence, and provide practical feedback to the design team.

  • Prepare and run development trials, including winding, joining, insulation and impregnation trials as assigned. Install instrumentation, commission rigs with engineers, take measurements and record what changed and what happened.

  • Investigate unexpected behaviour, propose practical fixes and work through build-test-modify iterations with engineers.

  • Organise the practical delivery of assigned projects: source small parts and consumables through agreed purchasing routes, arrange tools and build activities, and keep the workshop ready for use. Communicate progress, blockers and changing priorities to the lead technician.

  • Keep clear as-built records, annotated drawings, photographs, settings and trial observations so another technician can reproduce the work and understand each modification.

  • Transfer proven prototypes and methods to manufacturing or routine testing through initial work instructions, tooling, assembly sequences, training and technical handovers.

  • Work with engineers to identify hazards and establish the necessary risk assessments and controls before starting work on unproven hardware.

     

WHO YOU ARE

  • A technical apprenticeship or vocational qualification in mechanical, electrical, mechatronic or related engineering work, or equivalent hands-on experience.

  • Hands-on experience building, modifying and troubleshooting mechanical or electromechanical hardware in a workshop, laboratory, development or advanced manufacturing environment.

  • The ability to interpret engineering drawings, tolerances and 3D models, with working familiarity with geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) and practical measurement skills.

  • Confident hand-tool and workshop skills, sound fabrication and assembly judgement, and a willingness to develop unfamiliar techniques.

  • Resourcefulness with incomplete information: you investigate, ask useful questions, find suitable parts and propose a practical next step while keeping the engineering objective clear.

  • Sound judgement about technical uncertainty, safety and when a build or design change requires engineering review before proceeding.

  • The ability to organise work, adapt to agreed priority changes and document configurations and findings clearly.

  • Working English for technical discussions, drawings, instructions and build records.

Nice to have

  • Specialist fabrication skills such as manual or CNC machining, sheet-metal work, welding, brazing or additive manufacturing.

  • Experience creating or modifying simple parts and fixtures in CATIA, SolidWorks, Fusion 360 or similar CAD tools.

  • Experience with instrumentation, sensors, data acquisition, electrical wiring, vacuum, cryogenics or superconducting hardware.

  • Experience with composites, resins, vacuum bagging, insulation or impregnation.

  • Experience taking first-of-a-kind hardware or a prototype process through to repeatable manufacturing and technical handover.

  • German language skills.

 

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

  • CEO call (30 min)

 

This job would require frequent travels to our office in Villigen ( Zurich, CH)
*This role sits at "L3" of our framework, please inquire during the recruitment process for further information.

At Proxima Fusion, our mission is bold: making limitless clean energy a reality. To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

title: Field Account Executive - Bonn / Ruhrgebiet (w/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
Über uns & Die Opportunity

Bereit für die Freiheit, komplett eigenständig zu arbeiten, aber mit der Power eines globalen Tech-Pioniers im Rücken?
Lightspeed ist die führende All-in-One-Plattform für Handel und Gastronomie. Als KI-getriebenes Tech-Unternehmen bieten wir dir eines der besten SaaS-Produkte auf dem Markt.

In dieser Rolle bist du nicht einfach nur Angestellter – du bist der "Owner" deines eigenen Gebiets in Bonn oder Ruhrgebiet. Gemeinsam mit einem neuen, dynamischen Team von ca. 8 Personen und einem erfahrenen Manager vor Ort eroberst du den Gastronomiemarkt in deinem Gebiet. Wir verzichten auf Micromanagement und setzen auf Vertrauen, Freiheit und Ergebnisse.

Deine Mission in Bonn oder Ruhrgebiet

Du übernimmst die volle Verantwortung für dein Vertriebsgebiet und gewinnst die Top-Locations der Stadt für Lightspeed. Dein Erfolg basiert auf einem modernen, holistischen Vertriebsansatz:

  • Digitaler Rückenwind: Wir unterstützen dich aktiv durch Performance Marketing & qualifizierte Leads.

  • Strategische Partnerschaften: Du baust dir ein lokales Netzwerk und ein starkes Empfehlungsmanagement (Referrals) auf.

  • Gezielte Kaltakquise & Walk-ins: Du bist täglich im Markt präsent, besuchst Restaurants, Cafés sowie Bars und überzeugst die Inhaber direkt vor Ort.

  • Full-Cycle-Verantwortung: Du steuerst den gesamten Prozess selbstständig – vom ersten Händedruck über die Produkt-Demo bis zum erfolgreichen Vertragsabschluss.

  • Beratender Verkauf: Du verkaufst nicht nur Software, sondern hilfst Gastronomen partnerschaftlich dabei, ihr Business erfolgreicher zu machen.



Wer du bist (Dein Profil)

  • Ein echter Hunter: Du liebst die Herausforderung der Neukundengewinnung, bist extrem selbstmotiviert und brauchst niemanden, der dir ständig über die Schulter schaut.

  • Kommunikationsstark: Du sprichst Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau (essenziell für den Vertrauensaufbau mit lokalen Inhabern) und bringst gute Englischkenntnisse mit.

  • Charismatisch & Resistent: Du besitzt ein sicheres Auftreten, starke Präsentationsfähigkeiten und hast kein Problem damit, in ein volles Restaurant zu gehen und ein Gespräch zu starten.

  • Ehrgeizig: Du willst deinen Erfolg selbst in die Hand nehmen und suchst ein Umfeld, in dem Leistung direkt belohnt wird.

  • Erfahrung: Erste Erfahrung im Vertrieb, Business Development oder in der Gastronomie ist ein Plus – dein Drive und deine Einstellung zählen für uns jedoch am meisten.



Das Angebot – Warum Lightspeed?

  • Attraktives Vergütungspaket: Ein faires Fixgehalt gepaart mit einer ungedeckelten Provision (uncapped Commission) – mit überdurchschnittlich hohem Verdienstpotenzial für Top-Performer.

  • Regelmäßiger Gehalts-Boost: Eine echte Performance-Kultur, bei der dein Gehalt durch das Erreichen von klaren Umsatzmeilensteinen in schnellen Abständen spürbar steigen kann.

  • Sicherer Start: Wir investieren in dich. Freue dich auf einen erstklassigen Onboarding-Monat sowie eine strukturierte Ramp-up-Phase inklusive garantiertem Bonus in den ersten Monaten.

  • Company Equity: Werde durch unser attraktives Aktienprogramm direkt am Erfolg von Lightspeed beteiligt.

  • Lifestyle & Flexibilität: Profitiere von Vertrauensarbeitszeit, einem monatlichen Extra-Budget für Essen/Getränke sowie einem jährlichen Budget für Fitness und Wellness.

  • Team-Power & Kultur: Arbeite in einem großartigen lokalen Team in unserem NRW HQ und feiere unsere Erfolge bei legendären Events

  • Zusatzleistungen: Zuschuss zu deinem ÖPNV-Ticket für NRW sowie professionelle mentale Unterstützung über die Modern Health App.

 

Bewerb dich jetzt!

Lightspeed is a proud equal opportunity employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive and barrier-free workplace. Where to from here?

Obviously, this has to be mutually beneficial: we want you to step into a role you love, and we want to offer you a place you’re proud to come to every day. For a glimpse into our world check out our career page here.

Lightspeed is building communities through commerce, and we need people from all backgrounds and lived experiences to do that. The ethos of our business has been about inclusion from the very beginning, and we strive to provide a workplace where everyone belongs.

Powering the businesses that are the backbone of the global economy, Lightspeed's one-stop commerce platform helps merchants innovate to simplify, scale, and provide exceptional customer experiences. Our cloud commerce solution transforms and unifies online and physical operations, multichannel sales, expansion to new locations, global payments, financial solutions, and connection to supplier networks.

Founded in Montréal, Canada in 2005, Lightspeed is dual-listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: LSPD) and Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: LSPD). With teams across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, the company serves retail, hospitality, and golf businesses in over 100 countries.

title: [Field Sales - FR ] Account Executive Lyon (x/f/m)
descriptionHtml:
• Vos missions dans l'équipe commerciale

    La santé est l'une des choses les plus précieuses que nous ayons. Or, les soignants manquent parfois de temps et de moyens pour mener leur mission à bien.

    Chez Doctolib, nous voulons améliorer leur quotidien grâce à des services efficaces et innovants. Nos technologies les aident à réduire les tâches administratives pour libérer du temps médical, mieux soigner leurs patients, gagner en visibilité et développer leur activité.

    En tant que Business Developer, vous serez chargé de prendre contact sur le terrain avec les praticiens de votre zone et leur proposer les solutions Doctolib. Au quotidien, vos responsabilités incluent, mais ne sont pas limitées à :

    • Prospection terrain : décrocher des rendez-vous avec les professionnels de santé directement sur leur lieu de travail

    • Vente : écouter et comprendre les besoins des praticiens pour les convaincre d'adopter les solutions Doctolib (optimiser la gestion de leur pratique, gagner en visibilité, en temps médical et en confort)

    • Formation aux produits : assurer la formation des professionnels de santé à nos solutions au sein de leur cabinet

    • Reporting : utiliser le CRM Salesforce pour planifier vos tournées et tenir à jour le suivi administratif des clients

    Les qualités attendues pour ce poste

    Avant de poursuivre votre lecture, si vous n'avez pas le profil exact décrit ci-dessous, mais que vous pensez que cette description de poste correspond à vos compétences et à vos besoins, nous vous encourageons tout de même à postuler.

    Vous pourrez être le prochain membre de notre équipe si vous :

    • Avez déjà une expérience en prospection terrain notamment en porte-à-porte

    • Êtes passionné par la vente et motivé par les défis

    • Êtes autonome et savez gérer un cycle de vente complet (A à Z)

    • Avez une excellente communication orale et écrite

    • Êtes diplômé d'une école de commerce, d'une formation en vente ou équivalent universitaire (IUT/ BTS/ Licence commerciale)

    Ce serait fantastique si :

    • Vous cherchez un emploi qui a du sens : faciliter l'accès aux soins

    • Vous avez une appétence pour le monde du digital

    • Vous avez déjà utilisé un CRM

    Notre offre

    • Une mutuelle avantageuse prise en charge à 100 % par Doctolib pour les employés et leurs enfants

    • 25 jours de congés payés

    • Un programme de santé mentale et de coaching personnalisé gratuit avec notre partenaire Moka.care

    • Des tickets restaurant d'une valeur de 8,5 € par jour, dont 4,5 € pris en charge par Doctolib

    • Un programme d'intégration complet de 3 mois incluant la Doctolib Academy et diverses formations (langues, soft skills, compétences techniques)

    • Une subvention du comité d'entreprise pour le remboursement partiel d'adhésions à des activités sportives ou de loisirs

    • Un remboursement à 50 % de l'abonnement

    • Un congé supplémentaire au congé parental légal grâce au programme "Parent Care"

    • Pour les salariés en situation de handicap ou proches aidants, un package comprenant une adaptation du télétravail, des jours d'absence autorisée payés pour les rendez-vous médicaux et un soutien psychologique renforcé

    Le processus de recrutement

    • Entretien avec un recruteur : Un échange pour découvrir votre parcours, vos motivations et évaluer l'adéquation de vos compétences avec nos besoins.

    • Rencontre avec nos Managers : Une exploration de vos compétences à travers des mises en situation concrètes et une présentation de notre équipe et mission.

    • Échange avec nos Senior Managers : Un approfondissement de votre candidature incluant une simulation de prise de rendez-vous pour vous projeter dans le rôle.

    • Immersion dans notre équipe : Une demi-journée aux côtés d'un·e Business Developer pour vivre l'expérience Doctolib de l'intérieur et vous projeter dans votre futur rôle.

    • Prise de référence

    Détails du poste

    • CDI

    • Temps Plein

    • Zone : Lyon

    • Prise de poste : dès que possible

    • Rémunération : fixe + variable exponentiel et mensualisé

    Chez Doctolib, nous sommes convaincus que nous devons améliorer la santé pour tout le monde. Cela se reflète dans notre processus de recrutement. Nous évaluons les candidatures uniquement sur la base des qualifications et de la motivation, sans aucune forme de discrimination.

    Plus les idées sont diverses, plus notre produit améliorera véritablement la santé pour tout le monde. Vous pouvez postuler chez Doctolib, quel que soit votre genre, religion, âge, orientation sexuelle, origine ethnique ou handicap.

    Afin de garantir l'égalité des chances, nous vous invitons à exclure les informations personnelles (par exemple : photos, âge) de vos candidatures. Si vous avez besoin d'aménagements particuliers, merci de nous en informer pour que nous puissions adapter le processus de recrutement. Rejoignez-nous pour construire la santé dont nous rêvons tous !

    Toutes les informations fournies sont traitées par Doctolib pour la gestion des candidatures. Pour plus de détails sur le traitement des données, cliquez ici. Veuillez contacter hr.dataprivacy(at)doctolib.com pour toute question ou pour exercer vos droits.

title: Finance & Accounting Advisory - Managing Director
descriptionHtml:
Managing Director – Finance & Accounting Advisory

At CFGI, Managing Directors serve as key leaders in our organization, working closely with C-level executives at FTSE 100, mid-cap and start-up companies. As a Managing Director, you will take ownership of client relationships, drive engagement success, and play a pivotal role in the firm’s business development and growth strategies.

Take ownership of your career at CFGI:

  • Lead high-impact engagements across various industries and complex accounting topics.
  • Act as a strategic advisor to clients, providing expertise in technical accounting, transaction support, and regulatory reporting.
  • Build and manage long-term client relationships and expand CFGI’s market presence.
  • Drive firm initiatives, contribute to thought leadership, and mentor high-performing teams.

What you might expect:

  • Interact with clients’ executive team and auditors, serving as a subject matter expert, leading clients through complex accounting issues and driving conclusions.
  • Lead and oversee all aspects of client engagements, from scoping to execution, ensuring timely and high-quality deliverables.
  • Drive client deliverables of financial and regulatory information in accordance with regulatory requirements.
  • Drive business development initiatives by identifying new client opportunities, maintaining strong industry relationships, and actively participating in firm-wide growth strategies.
  • Mentor and develop professionals at all levels, fostering a culture of integrity, collaboration, and professional growth.
  • Develop and enhance the firm’s training programs, providing guidance on new accounting standards and best practices.

Who you are:

  • An undergraduate degree in Accounting – ACA, ACCA, CPA and/or MBA combined with solid accounting experience will be considered in lieu of a degree in accounting.
  • 14+ years of experience in accounting, finance, or consulting, including tenure at a Big 4 accounting firm.
  • Outstanding interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills with an ability to assimilate easily into teams.
  • Strong technical skills and a working knowledge of IFRS, UK GAAP and US GAAP.
  • Proactive in identifying client needs and effective in building a strong relationship with clients.
  • Highly organized and focused and demonstrates the ability to set overall engagement expectations and direction.
  • Effective analytical and critical thinking abilities.
  • Entrepreneurial nature, self-motivated, ethical, and dependable.
  • High energy with commitment to quality client service, focusing on ensuring positive resolutions to conflicts.
  • Consistently seek opportunities to enhance your skills by attending higher-level training, develop firm training materials and enhance overall firm knowledge base.

title: Finance Assistant
descriptionHtml:
Finance Assistant

Edinburgh

Wordsmith

Wordsmith is building the legal operations platform for in-house teams, and we’re growing fast.


We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents and disconnected systems.

Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgment matters, and every step is captured as work happens.

We’re built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend, and become a function the business can run with.

More than 500 companies use Wordsmith. We’ve raised over $80m from leading investors, and we’re building one of the defining companies in legal AI — from our office in Edinburgh.

Why this role is different

You won’t be joining a big, process-heavy finance function. You’ll be one of the first Finance hires, working on a brand new, AI-native ERP system (Rillet) with the freedom to actually improve how things are done — not just keep the lights on.

If you want real exposure to the business, a seat close to the founders and leadership team, and the chance to shape processes rather than inherit them, this is that seat.

The Role

As Finance Assistant, you’ll own the day-to-day mechanics that keep Wordsmith’s finances running — cash, invoicing, collections, payables and expenses — and you’ll have the tools and the licence to automate as much of it as possible.

What you'll do

  • Complete daily cash reconciliation across our accounts

  • Set up customer contracts in our ERP (Rillet) and issue invoices

  • Chase accounts receivable to keep debtor days down

  • Own all accounts payable activity, including uploading bills and creating payment runs

  • Help with month end balance sheet reconciliations

  • Help administer our travel and expense system

  • Pick up other finance tasks as they come up — in a small team, that’s part of the job

Who you might be

We’re not looking for someone who wants a narrow, ticket-based role. You might be:

  • Newly qualified, or qualified by experience, and ready to take real ownership from day one

  • 1–2 years post-qualified and looking for broader exposure than a larger finance function gives you

title: Finance Controller
descriptionHtml:
Finance Controller

Location: Netherlands

Start date: Q1 2027

Compensation: €70k - €80k annually (depending on experience)

Employment type: Full-time (contractor if outside Netherlands)

About DTACT

DTACT (Data Transform Act) is a data technology company that helps organizations transform complex information into clear, actionable insights. Founded in 2016, we work with government agencies and enterprises across Europe to solve critical data challenges and support better decision-making in areas such as cybersecurity, defense, intelligence, public safety, and critical infrastructure. Built on deep expertise in these domains, we develop innovative solutions that help organizations gain greater visibility, understanding, and control over their data.

As a fully remote and internationally distributed company, we combine technical excellence with a collaborative and adaptable way of working. Our mission is simple: to help organizations turn information into action, enabling faster, smarter decisions when they matter most.

The Role

We are looking for a Finance Controller to own DTACT’s finance function end-to-end as we continue to scale internationally. Reporting into the COO, you’ll take full ownership of accounting, collections, financial analytics, budgeting, and compliance (including our Dutch statutory obligations) — acting as the single point of accountability for finance in the business today. This is a hands-on, mid-level role: you’ll be expected to run the entire finance function largely on your own in the near term, while also bringing the leadership mindset and ambition to grow the function — and your own role — as DTACT expands.

What you'll do

  • Own end-to-end accounting operations — AP/AR, general ledger, and month end/year-end close — ensuring accurate, timely financial reporting.

  • Manage the full collections process: invoicing, aging follow-up, and cash flow forecasting.

  • Build and maintain finance analytics (dashboards, reports) that give leadership clear, real-time visibility into company performance.

  • Own the budgeting and forecasting cycle, partnering with department leads to track actuals against plan.

  • Ensure full compliance with Dutch tax and statutory reporting requirements (VAT, annual accounts) and manage relationships with external accountants, auditors, banks, and tax advisors.

  • Partner with People Operations on payroll processing and accuracy across jurisdictions, and own administration of the employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP).

  • Build and continuously improve finance processes, technical efficiencies and controls, laying the groundwork as the company grows.

What you'll bring

  • 5–8 years of progressive finance/accounting experience, including hands-on ownership of a full finance function — ideally within tech in a startup or scale-up environment.

  • Solid knowledge of Dutch accounting standards, tax regulations, statutory compliance requirements and payroll.

  • Proven ability to independently manage accounting, collections, budgeting, and financial analytics without a large supporting team.

  • Strong analytical skills and financial modeling ability; comfortable turning data into clear, actionable insights.

  • Leadership potential and genuine ambition to grow into a finance leadership role as the team and company scale.

  • A hands-on, “roll up your sleeves” attitude, paired with the ability to think and plan strategically.

  • Excellent communication skills in English and Dutch.

What's in for you

  • Competitive compensation and equity participation, including an Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP), allowing you to share in DTACT's long-term success.

  • Remote-first flexibility, with the opportunity to work from anywhere within compatible time zones and a schedule that supports both collaboration and personal needs.

  • A trust-based culture built around asynchronous communication, empowering people to work independently while staying connected and aligned across teams.

  • Generous time off, including vacation days and local public holidays to help you rest, recharge, and maintain a healthy work-life balance.

  • Home office support, including high-quality equipment and a budget to create a productive and comfortable workspace.

  • An international and diverse team, where English is our company language and collaboration spans multiple countries, backgrounds, and perspectives.

  • High-impact work: DTACT helps organizations in and outside the government with mitigating their vulnerabilities and providing alerts to incoming threats.

We believe diverse teams build better solutions.

DTACT welcomes applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of background or identity. We hire based on skills, experience, and potential, and encourage everyone who meets the role requirements to apply.

Please note: Visa sponsorship is not available for this role. Candidates must be authorized to work in their country of residence.

title: Forward deployed engineer, energy
descriptionHtml:
About Watershed

Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.

We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!

The role

Forward Deployed Energy Engineers are a new role at Watershed, combining energy and advisory expertise with product-building skills and commercial instinct. You’ll operate at the cutting edge with Watershed customers to build and deploy the next generation of enterprise energy management.

Energy is one of the largest costs on a big company’s P&L and one of its largest sources of emissions. Yet most enterprises have no one who owns how energy is purchased, consumed and reduced across all their sites. Watershed is building the product that changes that, and it’s the company’s biggest bet for its next chapter.

We already help many of the world’s largest companies measure and cut their emissions, and our clean energy business has executed more than $100M in purchases. Now we’re building energy management from zero to one, with engagements underway with a small group of customers today and scaling in 2027.

You’ll work with enterprises that spend tens of millions a year on electricity, embedded in their energy programmes. Starting from the energy data already in Watershed, you’ll find where they’re overspending, deliver the savings, prototype with AI what should become product, and help customers implement solutions, including buying clean power. The goal is an energy programme that wins backing from their CFO and facilities teams. This is a high-ownership role on a small, high-output team, with a direct line to commercial outcomes and real say in what we build. It reports directly to Watershed’s head of energy and decarbonization.

What you'll do

  • Deliver energy engagements with measurable results: Run deep engagements with a handful of customers at a time: change tariffs, upgrade equipment, find and cut waste, and show the savings.

  • Win customers who vouch for us: Earn the trust of facilities and finance leads so they would tell a peer to work with Watershed.

  • Turn what works into product: Spot the problems that repeat across customers, prototype with AI, and work with our engineers to build an AI-led product for many.

  • Close clean energy deals: Help customers sign deals with existing clean power products (eg EACs, fixed-price VPPAs), yourself or alongside our account teams.

  • Make the team smarter on energy: Be the person colleagues go to on tariffs, loads and what actually cuts a bill.

You might be a fit if you

  • Know how commercial and industrial sites use and buy energy (tariffs, loads, HVAC and controls, procurement) from time at an ESCO, an energy consultancy, an engineering firm or an energy-tech company.

  • Have built things: scripts, models, prototypes or AI-assisted workflows, and can show us one. Prototype-quality code is enough; moving fast matters most.

  • Are fluent with data tools (Excel, SQL or Python) and LLM tools, and can turn messy meter and bill data into something a customer acts on.

  • Have run client work from scoping to outcome, and are as credible with a facilities manager as with a CFO.

  • Can tell a compelling story with data, from raw numbers to insight to a recommendation someone signs off. You've originated work or supported deals, and want to get better at selling.

  • Are energised to build a new product and service, to be on the front lines of building a new business, and to leave a legacy as part of a fast-moving team.

Nice to have

  • Experience with clean power deals (PPAs, VPPAs, fixed-price power contracts, and energy attribute certificates like RECs, GOs and REGOs).

  • Hands-on work with utility bill, half-hourly or building management system data.

  • A few years in consulting or advisory.

Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles)

Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so.

What’s the interview process like?

It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process.

What if I need accommodations for my interview?

At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, mental health needs, religious observances, neurodivergence, or pregnancy-related support requirements. If you need assistance during your process, please contact your recruiter.

There are 36.5 million pets in UK homes, and 62% of households own one. Owners treat pets as family and spend like it: £11.95bn a year on pets and pet products. Yet every decision over a pet's life (which breed, what food, what training, which vet, what cover) is a separate search, and most new owners are learning as they go. Getting it wrong is expensive: vet prices rose 63% between 2016 and 2023, and UK pet insurers paid a record £1.23bn in claims in 2024.

General AI agents are going mainstream, but they only know what the owner remembers. We are building an agent that actually knows your pet. It starts before or on day one: helping you choose the right pet for your lifestyle, then guiding the first 100 days on nutrition, training and routine. Over time it learns your pet's breed, age, exercise and history, and shifts the focus to preventative care, so expensive problems are caught early or never happen. When something goes wrong ("my dog just ate chocolate, do I need a vet?"), it triages, connects you to a vet, and tells you what you're covered for before you book. Underneath sits a verified pet record that owners control and vets write to, so its advice starts from fact, not memory.

As Founder & CEO, you will be responsible for turning a strong thesis into a scaled, defensible business.

  • Pick the wedge. Decide where you win owners first: pre-purchase, the first 100 days, or a specific species or breed group, and prove they come back after the honeymoon period.

  • Build the agent people trust. Take the product from concept to an agent that gives genuinely useful, safe guidance on nutrition, training, prevention and triage, with vets and televet partners in the loop.

  • Make prevention pay. Show that better routines and earlier treatment reduce costly claims, and turn that into a model insurers and pet businesses will pay for.

  • Own the record. Build the verified pet record underneath, with owners' permission and vets writing to it, so the agent knows more than any general-purpose AI.

  • Launch with Aviva. Use Aviva's pet policyholders as early users and design a commercial partnership that works for both sides.

  • Build the company. Hire the initial team, raise capital, and establish the venture as the trusted companion for every pet owner in the UK, then beyond.

Your Ideal Experience:

The ideal candidate has built consumer products people love, ideally in pets, and knows how to use AI to do it.

  • Founder or early leader at a consumer pet business: pet insurance, pet care, televet, pet food or a pet subscription brand.

  • A strong consumer product instinct: you know how to acquire, activate and retain users, and you obsess over what keeps people coming back.

  • Comfortable building with AI: you can shape agentic products and work closely with engineers, even if you're not writing the code yourself.

  • Understanding of the vet ecosystem, pet health data or insurance is a strong plus.

  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity: shaping the product, defining the customer, and making irreversible calls with incomplete data.

  • Credibility with a large corporate partner and with forward-looking venture investors.

Most importantly, you care about pets and their owners, and want to build a company that keeps millions of them healthier for longer.

This is your company. We're here to help.

title: Front End Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Seamflow

Every plane, medical device, lift, battery and building has to be tested, inspected and certified before it reaches the world. It's the invisible layer that keeps the physical economy safe, and it still runs on Word documents, PDFs, spreadsheets and email. Seamflow is the software layer for that industry. We build AI-powered workflows for certification bodies, notified bodies and inspection companies: scheduling and resource planning, technical review, conformity assessment, field inspection, and document intelligence over messy real-world files.

Where we are:

  • Live in production inside some of the largest enterprises in the industry

  • $4.5M seed, 14x oversubscribed, co-led by Northzone and Initialized Capital, the funds behind Spotify, Klarna, Coinbase and Reddit. Angels include Charlie Songhurst and Mario Götze.

  • Demand is outstripping what we can build. That's the reason this role exists.

The team

Most of our engineers were olympiad medallists in maths, physics or informatics before they were engineers. The team has come to us from Google, Amazon, X, Yandex, McKinsey and Bain, and from founding-engineer seats at startups that went on to multi-billion-dollar valuations. We hire against a very high bar, and this role exists to raise it further.

The role

A Front End Design Engineer thinks in finished interfaces, not mockups or components in isolation. A technical reviewer at a notified body spends their day inside a 400-page technical file, cross-referencing clauses, checking test reports against standards, and deciding whether a medical device is safe to sell. Today they do that in Word, Acrobat and a spreadsheet someone built in 2011. The interface they use decides how fast they work and whether they trust the AI sitting next to them.

You own that interface. Layout, typography, interaction, motion, the design system underneath it, and the React that ships it. You decide how a reviewer sees a finding, how they correct a model that got it wrong, and how a hundred fields of dense regulatory data become something a person can actually read. You sketch it, build it, ship it, then sit next to someone using it and find out what you got wrong. You'll ship to production in your first week.

What we're looking for

We care far more about taste and engineering strength than about matching a list of tools. If you're excellent, we'll hire you whether you've spent the last three years in React, Svelte, Vue or something we haven't heard of. Our stack is learnable in a fortnight. Judgement, craft and speed are not.

What we're actually screening for:

  • You've designed and built an interface that real people used every day. Not a Dribbble shot, not a component library nobody adopted. Something that shipped, got used, and got better.

  • You have taste, and you can defend it. Typography, spacing, motion, hierarchy. You notice when something is a few pixels off and you can explain why it matters.

  • You build the whole thing. Design, frontend, the state and data it sits on. You don't hand the code to someone else once the Figma is done, and you don't hand the design to someone else once the code is.

  • You can design for density. Expert users, complex workflows, hundreds of fields on a screen. Making that clear is much harder than making a landing page beautiful.

  • You go to the source. You'll watch a technical reviewer work through a real file, and you'll design for what they actually do rather than what the process diagram says.

Signals we like, none of them required:

design engineering or front-end roles at somewhere like Linear, Vercel, Notion or Figma, a design system you built and maintained, work on interfaces where people review or correct AI output, founder or ex-founder, founding team experience, EF / YC / Antler, early or stealth-stage startup.

This is probably not for you if

  • You want a strict boundary between work and life. We run one of the most ambitious startup cultures in Europe: fast paced, extremely high ownership, and in person in Shoreditch.

  • You want a well-defined ticket handed to you each morning.

  • You want to specialise narrowly and stay in your lane.

What you get

  • Real equity, and compensation that reflects a high bar

  • Genuine ownership of product surface area from day one, with the founders in the room

  • Relocation support and visa sponsorship, handled properly

  • Lunch and dinner covered, 24/7 gym access, and any tool that makes you faster

  • A small team with high standards, high trust, and no politics

If this sounds like your kind of problem, apply. A short note on the hardest thing you've built goes further with us than a polished CV.

title: Generalist Architect
descriptionHtml:
TLDR; Davis is looking for an architect who has sized capacity across several programs, from light-industrial and logistics to residential, office and retail, and who wants to practice differently than in a traditional firm. Target experience: around 5 to 6 years.

About Davis

Davis is an AI-native real estate company accelerating early-stage development and architectural design. Today developers coordinate 4-5 fragmented stakeholders over weeks or months. Soon they'll need only one: Davis.

We turn every input that shapes a development decision into decision-ready outputs: investor-grade feasibility studies, investment analysis, and architect-certified designs, delivered in days. Every stage pairs our proprietary AI systems with expert review, so velocity never comes at the cost of reliability.

We closed a $5.5M pre-seed co-led by Heartcore Capital and Balderton Capital, with Yellow, Evantic and Entrepreneurs First, alongside angels from the founding teams of Spacemaker, Black Forest Labs, Hugging Face, Supabase, Cleo and Spore Bio. We already work with leading developers and expect to support hundreds of projects over the coming year, deepening our research, our hiring, and our coverage of the development process end to end.

The Role

Our clients come to us with a site and a capacity question, on a program that changes from one deal to the next. You are the one who answers whatever the program, and who stands behind the number in front of them.

You will run a portfolio of feasibility studies across light-industrial and logistics, residential, office, hospitality, retail and mixed-use operations. You take these projects from feasibility through schematic design.

This role sits at the meeting point of two worlds Davis is precisely working to bring together: architectural expertise and artificial intelligence. This is not a conventional architect position. It spans three complementary dimensions: guaranteeing the architectural quality and credibility of our deliverables, today generated in a matter of hours; co-producing the architectural drawings that accompany them; contributing actively to the development of our plan-generation technology.

It is an architect role whose impact reaches well beyond its own output.

The core of the role

  • Analyze local planning and zoning documents (land-use plans, development guidelines, easements) and derive project assumptions from them.

  • Set the programmatic assumptions for the program at hand, its ratios, structural grids and keys, and derive a quantified capacity.

  • Check and correct the outputs of our tools: confirm what holds up, fix what does not, and explain why.

  • Develop the project phase by phase, from a first capacity scenario through to a resolved project at schematic design.

  • Produce the graphic documents (drawings, images, diagrams) that make the project clear and compelling.

  • Arbitrate between several scenarios according to programmatic, regulatory and economic constraints.

  • Stand behind your numbers with the client, and defend them under challenge.

Contributing to the technology

  • Formalize best practice, program by program: translate ratios, structural grids and thresholds into criteria our AI teams can use.

  • Assess the model's outputs: say what is right, what is wrong, and on what grounds.

  • Work cross-functionally with the product, tech and real estate teams throughout the tool's continuous-improvement cycles.

Working as a team

  • Take part in project reviews and exchange with the other architects to improve methods and the quality of deliverables.

  • Contribute to the team's graphic standards.

What We're Looking For

  • Education: degree in architecture.

  • Experience: around 5 to 6 years. You have sized capacity yourself on at least three different programs (multi-family residential, logistics, light-industrial parks, office, hospitality or retail). Logistics or light-industrial is one of the three, as these are the programs that matter most to us. You know the ratios that govern each: clear height and loading docks in logistics and light-industrial, average area per unit and parking ratio in residential, structural grid and workstation ratio in office, area per key in hospitality.

  • Software: proficiency in Rhino and Revit is essential. AutoCAD is expected.

  • Appetite for digital tools and AI: the desire to bring them into your practice and to evolve it is essential. AI is one more tool in your hand, and drawing remains what we assess.

  • Speed and synthesis: our clients decide fast, on a number. You produce a credible, well-drawn scenario in hours, you cut to the essentials on ambiguous cases, and you know what level of detail serves the decision at each phase.

Core skills

  • Buildable capacity: connect a zoning rule to its quantified effect on a volume, and a volume to a program.

  • Programmatic versatility: move from residential to office, to logistics warehouse, to light-industrial or hospitality, and grasp the logic of each quickly.

  • Planning documents and how they apply: building envelope, height, setbacks, spacing rules, footprint, planted open ground, parking, permitted uses.

  • Site plan: siting, access, parking, water management, integration and edges.

  • Project phases, from feasibility through schematic design, and the level of detail each one requires.

  • Production of graphic documents: plans, sections and diagrams that make a capacity rationale legible to an investor.

Complementary skills

  • Rigor and a sense of synthesis, especially on ambiguous cases.

  • Information structuring: organizing what you produce so that others, human or machine, can use it.

  • Ability to work cross-functionally with the product, tech and real estate teams.

Why join Davis?

  • Take part in a genuine transformation of the real estate profession, and co-build the next generation of feasibility standards alongside a high-caliber technical team.

  • Go through a volume and a diversity of programs a traditional firm cannot offer.

  • See your work in every deliverable, and correct the tool when it gets things wrong.

  • Join a young company where methods and tools are still being built, and where your expertise shapes the way we work.

Package

  • Fixed-term or permanent contract depending on the case, to be discussed together

  • Offices in the center of Paris 2e

  • Company health insurance covered

  • Meal vouchers

  • Sports membership covered

  • 50% reimbursement of public transport

More information about Davis, the team and the market we’re going after:

Team

Mehdi (CEO) grew up in a family of architects and has lived this problem firsthand. He's a repeat founder who bootstrapped his first startup at 20, and graduated from Sciences Po and HEC Paris. Amine (CTO) is an AI researcher from École Polytechnique who worked extensively on discrete diffusion and turned down a PhD with Google DeepMind to build Davis. They started working together in July 2025 at Entrepreneur First's first European residency, a two-month lock-in in a German castle.

Today we're a team of 12: technical profiles from Polytechnique, ENS and INRIA alongside architects and deep real estate expertise.

We're small with an extremely high bar. If you want to work deeply on hard problems and see your work reach clients within days, you're the one we need.

Why We'll Win

Real estate is a $13 trillion industry that technology has largely bypassed. The professional services that feed it (design, engineering, feasibility, permitting) represent hundreds of billions in spend that no one has seriously automated.

Proptech spent the last decade selling SaaS on the edges of these workflows. It didn't work, for two reasons: no professional wants another tool to learn, and no tool can automate work that runs on expert judgment. Davis makes a different bet. We don't sell tools, we sell the work: AI-generated, expert-validated, delivered in days instead of weeks. Every project compounds our data advantage across typologies, geographies and regulatory contexts.

We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV.

If you're drawn to what we're building but don't meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet 100% of the criteria. If that's you, please don't let that hold you back. We'd love to receive your application.

title: Grid Systems Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Description

Hyperscale Power is building the power backbone for the AI data center era: a complete power conversion chain from 13.8kV–35kV medium-voltage AC down to 800V DC, combining ultra-compact SiC-based AC/DC and DC/DC power blocks. The grid interconnection is where our system meets the utility – getting it right is fundamental to a safe, compliant and reliable product across every market we serve.

As Grid Systems Engineer, you will design and develop the medium-voltage grid interconnection aspects of our power conversion system – from prototype construction and checkout through certification and volume production. You will work closely with the Power Electronics, Firmware and Test & Field teams, and with our external test & certification partners, to ensure our systems meet grid codes and interconnection requirements across our target markets.

It is a unique opportunity to shape the grid interface of a breakthrough power electronics platform from an early stage – with direct visibility to the CTO and engineering leadership.

Key Responsibilities

• Design and develop the medium-voltage (13.8kV–35kV) grid interconnection system and related electromechanical/electronic equipment; prepare related installation, operation and maintenance specifications and instructions.

• Analyze equipment to establish operating data and conduct experimental tests on grid-interface hardware (transformers, protection, switchgear interfaces) under realistic grid conditions.

• Analyze engineering proposals and technical data to determine the feasibility of new equipment or modifications to existing designs for different grid voltage levels and markets.

• Responsible for prototype construction and checkout of grid-interconnection subsystems, supporting our Prototype and Alpha Customer milestones.

• Compile operational data and prepare customer application information and documentation for grid-tied deployments.

• Ensure compliance with grid codes, interconnection standards and utility requirements (e.g., IEEE 519, IEEE 1547, IEC 61850, UL 1741) and support certification processes together with our test & certification partners (UL, TÜV, IEC 62477).

• Collaborate with the Power Electronics and Firmware teams on protection coordination, fault ride-through, and control strategies for grid-tied operation.

• Respond to customer and partner technical requests regarding grid interconnection requirements as they occur.

• Support scaling of the grid-interface design across different grid codes and markets as we move from Alpha Customer readiness to Production and Volume Readiness.

Qualifications

• BSc / MSc in electrical engineering, power systems engineering or comparable education.

• Experience in medium-voltage grid interconnection, power systems, or utility-scale grid-tied power electronics (e.g. solar/wind/BESS inverters, solid-state transformers) preferred.

• Familiarity with grid codes and interconnection standards (e.g. IEEE 519, IEEE 1547, IEC 61850, IEC 61400, IEC 62933, VDE-AR-N, UL 1741).

• Hands-on experience with prototype build, checkout and test of electromechanical/electronic equipment.

• Strong analytical skills; comfortable designing and running experimental tests, analyzing the resulting data, and documenting the results.

• Team player, comfortable engaging directly with customers and partners on technical requirements.

• Language skills: fluent in English, spoken and written; German language skills helpful, but not mandatory.

• The job will be located at our HQ in Egg b. Zürich in Switzerland. National and international willingness to travel is assumed.

Benefits

• Equity + competitive salary.

• Unique technology and market opportunity – validated prototype and first paying customers on the path to volume shipments.

• Hybrid work with flexible working times.

title: Hardware Engineer, FPGA
descriptionHtml:
Normal Computing | Build with Us

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), and London.

The Role

Validating conventional silicon is a solved discipline. Validating silicon that computes with noise is not, and you will be the one who figures out how. As our FPGA Design Engineer, you will own the bridge between RTL and physical silicon: bringing our physics-inspired ASIC designs to life on FPGA platforms for pre-silicon validation and early software development, and building the test infrastructure for post-silicon bring-up and characterization. Your scope spans the entire FPGA lifecycle: selecting hardware platforms, implementing complex RTL, debugging in the lab, and writing the software that drives it all, working daily with our silicon, EDA, and research teams.

What You Will Own

  • FPGA Platform Ownership: Lead the selection, procurement, and bring-up of FPGA prototyping platforms (e.g., HAPS, VCU118/VPK180-class boards, or custom hardware) for pre-silicon RTL validation and software development.

  • RTL Implementation: Adapt and implement complex ASIC RTL onto FPGA targets, including multi-clock-domain architectures, CDC bridges, and timing closure on dense designs.

  • IP Integration: Integrate in-house designs with third-party and vendor IP; serve as the expert on the AMD/Xilinx ecosystem (Vivado IP Integrator, transceivers, memory controllers).

  • High-Speed Interfaces: Design, implement, and validate high-speed I/O with a focus on PCIe: our accelerators ship as PCIe cards in standard servers.

  • Post-Silicon Validation: Build FPGA-based "tester" designs for silicon bring-up, device characterization, and automated test environments.

  • Hardware-Software Stack: Develop the software layer around the hardware: Python/C++ hardware abstraction, register-map generation, and automated build and regression flows.

  • Lab Debug: Root-cause complex timing and functional issues in real time using ILA/Vivado Analyzer, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and BER/eye-diagram characterization of high-speed links.

What Makes You a Great Fit

  • Proven industry experience taking FPGA designs from RTL through timing closure to validated hardware, ideally in an ASIC prototyping, emulation, or high-growth hardware environment.

  • Expert-level SystemVerilog and/or VHDL for synthesis, with deep proficiency in Xilinx Vivado (synthesis, place & route, timing closure, IP catalog).

  • Hands-on experience implementing and debugging PCIe, plus AXI/AHB, SPI, UART, JTAG, and other common interfaces.

  • Strong Python for automation, test, and build tooling.

  • Strong board-level bring-up and lab debugging skills on real hardware.

  • Startup mindset: you work independently, pivot quickly, and run at ambiguous problems that span hardware, software, and physics.

Bonus Points

  • Verification frameworks like Cocotb or UVM

  • Experience deploying ML models to FPGAs (hls4ml, FINN, or custom NN-to-RTL flows), or building real-time, sub-microsecond signal processing pipelines.

  • Mixed-signal ASIC exposure: digital front-ends, ADC/DAC interfaces, or analog compute.

  • SERDES tuning and signal integrity fundamentals.

title: hbo-stage Bedrijfskunde: Digitalisering en Procesoptimalisatie van communicatie
descriptionHtml:
hbo-afstudeerstage, vanaf februari 2027

Ben jij die enthousiaste hbo-student die het leuk vindt om organisatievraagstukken te onderzoeken en processen te verbeteren?

Dit is jouw uitdaging

Het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS) wil het gebruik van papieren post verminderen en de mogelijkheden voor digitale communicatie verder uitbreiden. Dit geldt zowel voor de communicatie met bedrijven als met personen. Tijdens deze stage richt je je specifiek op de communicatie met individuele onderzoekspersonen.

Op dit moment benadert het CBS onderzoekspersonen in eerste instantie vrijwel altijd via een brief op het huisadres. Digitale communicatie, bijvoorbeeld via e-mail, biedt kansen om dit proces efficiënter, flexibeler en toekomstbestendiger in te richten. Er lopen binnen het CBS al verschillende initiatieven om meer gebruik te maken van e-mailadressen, maar er zijn ook nog belangrijke vraagstukken die onderzocht moeten worden.

Denk bijvoorbeeld aan de volgende vragen:

  • Hoe kan het CBS op een effectieve manier e-mailadressen van onderzoekspersonen verzamelen en beheren?

  • Welke juridische en privacyvoorwaarden gelden voor het opbouwen en gebruiken van een e-maildatabase?

  • Welke technische aanpassingen en voorzieningen zijn nodig om digitale communicatie mogelijk te maken?

  • Hoe moeten de bestaande werkprocessen worden aangepast om digitale communicatie goed te ondersteunen?

  • Hoe kunnen we ervoor zorgen dat onderzoekspersonen op een toegankelijke en betrouwbare manier digitaal benaderd worden?

Samen met het Waarneeminnovatie Team en collega's van de afdeling Dataverzameling ga je dit vraagstuk onderzoeken. Je brengt de huidige situatie in kaart, onderzoekt mogelijkheden voor verbetering en werkt toe naar concrete aanbevelingen voor het CBS.

Dit is jouw stageplek bij CBS Heerlen

Je gaat aan de slag in het Team Waarneeminnovatie. Dit team valt binnen de afdeling Dataverzameling. We zijn een jong, divers en vooral enthousiast team dat als doel heeft de waarneming van het CBS te vernieuwen en te verbeteren.

Dit breng jij mee

Je volgt een hbo-opleiding Bedrijfskunde of een soortgelijke opleiding.

  • Je hebt interesse in procesoptimalisatie, digitalisering en organisatieverandering.

  • Je bent nieuwsgierig, onderzoekend en neemt graag initiatief.

  • Je vindt het leuk om met verschillende betrokkenen binnen een organisatie in gesprek te gaan.

  • Je hebt een proactieve, positieve en assertieve houding en denkt in oplossingen, staat open voor feedback en gaat uitdagingen met enthousiasme aan.

Omdat tijdens de stage alle communicatie – zowel mondeling als schriftelijk – in het Nederlands plaatsvindt, is een goede beheersing van de Nederlandse taal noodzakelijk.

Dit kun je van ons verwachten

Een fijne leeromgeving waarin je:

  • samen met ervaren vakmensen bestaande processen analyseert en verbeterkansen herkent;

  • zelfstandig een praktijkgericht onderzoek of experiment opzet;

  • aan de slag gaat met het in kaart brengen van verschillende organisatorische, juridische en technische belangen en randvoorwaarden rondom digitale communicatie;

  • leert om onderzoeksresultaten te vertalen naar concrete, onderbouwde en uitvoerbare aanbevelingen voor het CBS.

Voor jouw inzet ontvang je een stagevergoeding van € 800,- bruto per maand (op basis van 40 uur per week).

Samen met je stagebegeleider stem je af hoe je hybride kunt werken, met flexibele werktijden en de optie om deels vanuit huis aan jouw stageopdracht te werken.

Dit zijn onze voorwaarden

Het betreft een stageopdracht en geen werkervaringsplek. Voordat je aan de stage begint verwachten we dat je vanuit de onderwijsinstelling een stagebegeleider hebt, waarmee de stage is afgestemd en concrete leerdoelen zijn afgesproken.
Deze stageopdracht is bedoeld voor studenten die momenteel staan ingeschreven bij een onderwijsinstelling; afgestudeerden komen niet in aanmerking.
